newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge dismisses final DeLorean fraud claim.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge dismisses final DeLorean fraud claim.

text.p: A federal judge on Tuesday dismissed the final securities fraud claim remaining in two lawsuits against Arthur Andersen & Co., that dealt with the firm's auditing activities for the bankrupt DeLorean Motor Company.
The suits were filed against the accounting firm by the Department of Economic Development, a British government agency, and the trustee for the bankrupt company.

At issue in the lawsuits was whether the government agency "made a new investment decision for federal securities law purposes when it agreed in 1980 to revise the terms of a put (arrangement) it held with respect to preference shares of DeLorean Motor Corporation."

In dismissing the claim, U.S. District Judge Michael Mukasey said "the put revision did not cause government agencies to make a purchase or sale of a security within the meaning" of federal securities law. Since no more federal claims existed in the suits, the remaining state claims were also thrown out.
However, Judge Mukasey left open the possibility that the agency and trustee could refile their state claims in New York state court.

The suits arose out of 1978 agreement by DeLorean Motor to build sports cars in Northern Ireland. Andersen's role was to certify the company's financial statements in the agreement by the British government agency to invest 17.8 million pounds into the project and to extend 44.9 million pounds more in grants, loans and loan guarantees. But DeLorean Motor collapsed in 1981 and later sought bankruptcy-law protection.

"We look forward to trying the case in state court and for a quick trial on the merits. No decision has been made on whether we will appeal today's ruling by Judge Mukasey," Robert Sidorsky, one of the attorneys for the Department of Economic Development.
Attorneys for the accounting firm could not immediately be reached.
